name: Fugazi
label: Dischord
lede: Six albums, a five-dollar ticket, more than a thousand shows across all fifty states, and not one official T-shirt for sale.

eras.title: A word from a war book
eras.text: Minor Threat and Embrace were behind Ian MacKaye, and he wanted something slower, heavier and less shouted. The band took a year to find its shape: Joe Lally, who'd been hauling Beefeater's gear, a drummer swap from Colin Sears to Brendan Canty, and Guy Picciotto, who kept showing up to practice until he was in.

years.h: Ian MacKaye finds a bass player on Beefeater's crew
years.p: [[Joe Lally|62046ffd-7d76-476b-bee5-b281b7575c6c]] had been roadying for [[Beefeater|8c016ef4-0d18-4795-86dd-35ec90a509c9]]. He, Ian MacKaye and [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] drummer [[Colin Sears|c9bbc03c-06bf-4c37-9f54-e95b51aede4c]] start practicing as Fugazi.
years.xp: The name comes from Mark Baker's Vietnam oral history Nam, where fugazi means false, fake, not right.

years.h: Colin Sears out, [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] in on drums
years.p: Former [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] drummer Brendan Canty replaces Colin Sears. Within months Canty's old Rites of Spring bandmate [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]] is singing with Fugazi too.

years.h: Fugazi's first show: the Wilson Center, five dollars at the door
years.p: A $5 benefit for Dischord's State of the Union comp, with [[Marginal Man|fff14e91-ae03-4105-8fbb-3a318d6c01ca]], Ignition and Fire Party. About 300 people come; Fugazi play as a three-piece, with Waiting Room already in the set.
years.xp:
The flyer drew [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]] waiting on Ian MacKaye, Joe Lally and Brendan Canty, a joke that turned out to be a forecast. It was one of the rare nights Fugazi played as a trio and one of the rare nights they weren't the headliner.

The door price stuck. Five dollars became the band's target for the rest of its life, worked out on an early tour as the lowest price that could still pay for the trip.

Joey Picuri rolled a cassette that night, the first of hundreds of Fugazi shows he taped.

years.h: Guy Picciotto starts singing with Fugazi
years.p: Guy Picciotto is singing with Fugazi by the band's second show. Once his other band, [[Happy Go Licky|4c18be5e-2e53-41a4-a4a1-d9080ff88f8c]], winds down, Ian MacKaye asks him to join for good.

eras.title: Seven songs and a van to Europe
eras.text: Fugazi went from a D.C. rumor to a working touring band in two years. They cut their records at Don Zientara's Inner Ear in Arlington, gave music away at shows, and learned the hard way that a first album can go in the bin.

years.h: Fugazi, a.k.a. 7 Songs · Dischord No. 30
years.p: Recorded in June with [[Ted Niceley|fbe203ef-a327-4d7e-af16-a10d55b7347d]]. Ian MacKaye plays every guitar note and Guy Picciotto only sings.
years.xp: The cover was shot at Maxwell's in Hoboken on June 30, 1988. The drop into silence 22 seconds into Waiting Room became the band's calling card.

years.h: Margin Walker: what survived Fugazi's scrapped debut LP
years.p: After a grinding European tour, Fugazi made a first full-length in December 1988 that nobody in the band liked. Six of its songs survive as Margin Walker, Dischord No. 35.

years.h: Recording Repeater around Ted Niceley's culinary school
years.p: Fugazi make Repeater at Inner Ear, but producer Ted Niceley is in culinary school, so the band can only work with him from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.

years.h: 13 Songs puts both Fugazi EPs on one disc
years.p: Dischord No. 36 pairs 7 Songs with Margin Walker. For a lot of listeners, this is where Fugazi starts.

eras.title: Everyone wants in. Nobody gets in.
eras.text: Two guitars now, a punishing road schedule, and a crowd that outgrew every room. The bigger Fugazi got, the more the industry circled, and the more the band's rules (all ages, cheap tickets, Dischord only) became the story.

years.h: Repeater · Dischord No. 44
years.p: Fugazi's first full album, and the first with Guy Picciotto on guitar, a trebly Rickenbacker cutting against Ian MacKaye's.
years.xp: Jim Saah shot the cover. Between March 1990 and June 1991 the band played around 250 shows.

years.h: Fugazi refund violent slam-dancers $5 and walk them out
years.p: Ian MacKaye would stop a song and politely ask slam-dancers who were hurting people to cut it out. If they kept at it, Wikipedia says, Fugazi had them walked out and handed a $5 refund in an envelope.

years.h: Fugazi play Lafayette Park, facing the White House
years.p: Days before Desert Storm, Fugazi play a free Gulf War protest show in Lafayette Park, in rain and sleet, that also backed D.C.'s homeless. The set later turns up in the film Instrument.
years.xp:
It was part of a wider punk percussion protest against the coming war. Fugazi played directly in front of the White House. The Live Series logs the crowd at 1,500; the notes on the same page put it nearer 3,000.

Joey Picuri taped it, like almost everything else. It's in the Live Series today, sleet and all.

years.h: Steady Diet of Nothing · Dischord No. 60
years.p: Ted Niceley has become a chef and turns the job down, so Fugazi produce themselves for the first time, with [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] engineering. The album lands about two months before Nirvana's Nevermind changes the weather.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, 13 Songs and Repeater had sold more than 300,000 copies between them by summer 1991, and Steady Diet of Nothing had over 160,000 advance orders six months before release.

years.h: In on the Kill Taker · Dischord No. 70
years.p: Their first record to reach the Billboard 200, peaking at No. 153, on a label that ran out of a house in Arlington.

q: I would never trade what we had for what Nirvana had
years.src: Louder (Paul Brannigan) · Wikipedia (citing Our Band Could Be Your Life) · Dischord
years.h: Atlantic's Ahmet Ertegun comes backstage at Roseland
years.p: Fugazi sell out three nights at New York's Roseland Ballroom, and Atlantic Records chief Ahmet Ertegun, who signed Led Zeppelin and the Rolling Stones, is in the dressing room. Fugazi say no.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Ertegun offered them anything they wanted, their own subsidiary label and more than $10 million. Louder, from Paul Brannigan's interviews for MOJO, reports the same figure plus a promise of creative control; Ertegun even brought up his old deal with the Stones. Guy Picciotto called signing the most stupid and self-destructive thing they could have done. Lollapalooza wanted Fugazi to headline its 1993 tour too; they passed.

Ian MacKaye's reason was control: once a major was in, the band would be compromised. Fugazi managed itself and kept its records on Dischord, which meant no one else got a say in what a ticket or an album cost.

years.h: "Brendan #1" live in Washington DC, August 7, 1993

eras.title: Slower, stranger, and on film
eras.text: Instead of chasing the sound that got them there, Fugazi started taking it apart in the studio: clarinet, samples, a boombox, two drum kits. At the same time, Ian MacKaye's old high-school friend Jem Cohen was cutting ten years of Super 8 footage of the band into a film.

years.h: Red Medicine · Dischord No. 90
years.p: Self-produced at Inner Ear and a house in Guilford, Connecticut, it opens on a boombox recording and pulls back from the In on the Kill Taker punch.
years.xp: The tour behind it ran 172 dates, from March 1995 to November 1996.

years.h: The bootleg shirt that said it wasn't a Fugazi shirt
years.p: A Boston T-shirt maker sells a bootleg printed "This is not a Fugazi T-shirt." Ian MacKaye tracks him down and, instead of suing, asks him to give the profits to a community group.
years.xp:
Louder tells it this way: the bootlegger picked Rosie's Place, a Boston shelter for homeless women, and gave the shirt money there until he closed up shop. MacKaye asked him to be as creative with his accounting as he'd been with the design.

MacKaye later called him a smart motherfucker. Fugazi never sold an official shirt, then or since.

years.h: End Hits · Dischord No. 110
years.p: Seven months at Inner Ear, with Brendan Canty stacking two drum kits over a drum machine. Fans read the title as a goodbye; it was a joke about the drum hits after the last track.

years.h: Former roadie [[Jerry Busher|59c39d46-efd2-4fa0-912e-93ead7a4ab97]] becomes Fugazi's second drummer
years.p: To play the layered End Hits drums live, Fugazi bring in their former roadie Jerry Busher on a second kit alongside Brendan Canty.

years.h: Instrument: ten years on Super 8, 16mm and video
years.p: Jem Cohen, who met Ian MacKaye in high school, cuts a decade of Fugazi footage into a film that plays more like a diary than a rock doc.
years.xp: The footage runs from 1987 to 1998, on Super 8, 16mm and video. The Instrument Soundtrack (Dischord No. 120) came out alongside it, mostly instrumentals and unreleased demos.

eras.title: The best album, then the door
eras.text: Fugazi made what a lot of fans rank as their best record almost fifteen years in, then barely toured it. Families and other lives were pulling at them, and the last run of shows ended in London without anyone announcing it as the end.

years.h: The Argument · Dischord No. 130
years.p: For the first time Fugazi bring in outside players: Jerry Busher on percussion, Kathi Wilcox of [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]] and Bridget Cross of [[Unrest|f444dc7d-59c1-4ed6-beb7-f90b6d85366c]] on backing vocals, Amy Domingues on cello.
years.xp: Recorded January to April 2001 at Inner Ear and Dischord House. The Furniture + 2 EP came out alongside it.

years.h: Fugazi play just 32 shows in two years
years.p: For a band that once played 250 shows in fifteen months, Fugazi slow to a crawl as the four members make room for families and other projects.

years.h: Three sold-out nights at the London Forum, then Fugazi stop
years.p: Fugazi's last night at the Forum, November 4, runs two encores and ends on Glueman. Nobody billed it as the final show, but it was.
years.xp:
Buff Medways and Winnebago Deal opened that last night.

The band never announced a split. Dischord's own line is an indefinite hiatus, dated 2003, and the members have said since that they aren't broken up.

Nick Pellicciotto recorded the last night. In May 2025 it was one of the first two full shows Fugazi put on streaming services, paired with the Wilson Center tape from 1987.

eras.title: Not broken up, just not playing
eras.text: No reunion tour, no festival payday. Instead Fugazi opened the vault: nearly every show they ever played, priced the way their tickets were. Meanwhile the four of them kept making music in other bands, sometimes with each other.

q: It doesn't really become a song until it goes into someone else's ears
years.h: The Fugazi Live Series: every tape, five dollars suggested
years.p: Dischord launches an online archive of Fugazi shows priced on a sliding scale from $1 to $100. Ian MacKaye identified unlabeled tapes by clues like the accents in the crowd.
years.xp:
Joey Picuri and others had taped the band from the very first show, and MacKaye admitted the band had barely listened to them. The site grew to document more than a thousand shows with close to 900 recordings.

The same year, MacKaye said the band had turned down enormous reunion offers. Bassist Joe Lally was living in Rome by then.

years.h: Ian MacKaye: money won't bring Fugazi back
years.p: Asked about reunion offers, Ian MacKaye is blunt: Fugazi have been offered a lot, and money isn't what would bring them back.
years.xp: He said it wasn't going to be money that brought them back. The only reason to play again would be wanting to, and the schedules lining up across two continents. That position hasn't moved.

years.h: First Demo: Fugazi's 1988 giveaway tape, out at last
years.p: In January 1988 Fugazi cut eleven songs at Inner Ear and handed ten out free on cassette at shows. Dischord releases the full session in 2014 as No. 181.
years.xp: The eleventh song, Turn Off Your Guns, never made the original cassette. The session had sat in a drawer for more than 25 years.

years.h: Brendan Canty and Joe Lally start [[The Messthetics|62788614-b33c-42c9-9b6e-c9375362b57e]]
years.p: An instrumental trio with guitarist Anthony Pirog. The Fugazi rhythm section, Canty on drums and Lally on bass, back in a room together.

years.h: Ian MacKaye and Joe Lally form [[Coriky|d471b090-3866-4cf3-b8a0-476e11f30a58]] with Amy Farina
years.p: [[Amy Farina|30d1b9a6-4156-49ec-84ba-65c3f5ebbf69]], Ian MacKaye's partner in [[The Evens|3a3b3e5d-2d28-4108-875e-30686d2710e8]], joins him and his old Fugazi bassist. Coriky's debut album, set for March, gets pushed to June as the pandemic shuts independent record stores.

years.h: Fugazi finally on streaming
years.p: The Fugazi Live Series starts landing on Bandcamp and streaming services, beginning with the first show (Wilson Center, 1987) and the last (London Forum, 2002).

years.h: Albini Sessions: Fugazi's shelved 1992 album, out at last
years.p: In fall 1992 Fugazi recorded In on the Kill Taker with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] in Chicago, then shelved it with his blessing and remade it at home. The Chicago tapes come out in 2026 as a Bandcamp benefit.
years.xp:
After hearing the rough mixes, the band redid the album at Inner Ear with Don Zientara and Ted Niceley. The Chicago tapes sat in the vault for 33 years before coming out as a name-your-price download, with proceeds to Letters Charity, a cause Albini backed.

Albini didn't live to see it: he died of a heart attack in May 2024, at 61.
